title: Reading Drill — Recording visitors' questions at a museum — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Recording visitors' questions at a museum — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Ravensmere, work on volunteers giving different answers to the same question had already produced a small collection of anonymous notes. The education team used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: agreement between replies.

**B** The group kept a collection of agreed explanations for the new trial, which was planned to run for seven weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that different tour lengths should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
